hints.title: Use the kite structure
hints.body: The diagonal through the vertices where equal adjacent sides meet is perpendicular to the other diagonal. Mark the right angles this gives at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi></mrow></math>.
hints.recap: A kite supplies perpendicular diagonals, but its two diagonal lengths need not be equal.
hints.pitfall: Do not infer extra equalities from the appearance of the drawing.
hints.pause: Identify the smaller right triangles that contain the sides of triangle SPQ.

recall.reminder: A necessary and sufficient condition must work in both directions.

hints.title: Compute squared side lengths
hints.body: Use the small right triangles to express <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>S</mi><msup><mi>P</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><msup><mi>Q</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> in terms of the labelled lengths. Also express the whole length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>Q</mi></mrow></math>.
hints.recap: Pythagoras relates the squared lengths of a right triangle.
hints.pitfall: Add the two collinear lengths to obtain SQ before squaring it.
hints.pause: Write the three expressions needed to test whether triangle SPQ is right-angled at P.

recall.reminder: Draw or identify the triangles that contain the lengths required by the question.

hints.title: Use the converse as well as the theorem
hints.body: Triangle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi></mrow></math> is right-angled at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> exactly when <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>S</mi><msup><mi>P</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi><msup><mi>Q</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>S</mi><msup><mi>Q</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math>. Substitute your expressions and simplify.
hints.recap: The converse of Pythagoras supplies the reverse implication here.
hints.pitfall: Expand the square of a sum with its cross term.
hints.pause: Derive the condition in x, y and z and check that every algebraic step is reversible.

recall.reminder: Establish necessity and sufficiency, not just one implication.

solution:
The kite diagonals meet perpendicularly at O, so SP2=x2+z2, PQ2=x2+y2, and SQ=y+z.

By Pythagoras and its converse, the angle at P is right exactly when (x2+z2)+(x2+y2)=(y+z)2. Expanding and cancelling gives 2x2=2yz, or x2=yz. Every step is reversible.

Answer: C.
knowledgePattern: Use the kite diagonals and Pythagoras in both directions
